By letter dated July 31, 2025 (Reference 1), Constellation Energy Generation, LLC (CEG)
submitted a license amendment request (LAR) to make certain changes to the Renewed Facility
License (RFL) DPR 50 for the Christopher M. Crane Clean Energy Center, (CCEC). Specifically,
CEG requested an amendment to revise the RFL and Appendix A, Technical Specifications
(TSs) to support resumption of power operations at CCEC.

The NRC staff has determined that additional information is needed to complete the review of
the LAR submitted in Reference 1. The NRCs Final Request for Additional Information (RAI)
was provided to CEG in Reference 2.

temporary requirement until the Renewed Facility Operating License (RFOL) and TSs for the

restoration of the operating reactor licensing basis.

Attachment 4 includes additional detail in support of deleting LC.2.c.(23) and LC 2.c.(24). The
proposed markup of the affected RFOL pages is provided in Attachment 5.

There are no regulatory commitments contained in this letter.

By application dated July 31, 2025 (Agencywide Documents Access and Management System
Accession No. ML25212A076), Constellation Energy Generation, LLC (CEG, the licensee),
submitted a license amendment request to make certain changes to the Renewed Facility
License (RFL) DPR-50 for the Christopher M. Crane Clean Energy Center, (CCEC).
Specifically, CEG requested an amendment to revise the RFL and Appendix A, Technical
Specifications (TSs) to support resumption of power operations at CCEC.

The following requests for additional information (RAI) are needed for the NRC staff to complete
the technical review. The NRC staff requested as part of the submitted response, to provide a
markup of the affected pages for the staffs review. The markup of the affected pages are
included in Attachment 2.

Requirement:

Section 50.90, Application for amendment of license, construction permit, or early site permit,
of 10 CFR requires that whenever a licensee desires to amend the license, an application for an
amendment must be filed with the Commission fully describing the changes desired and
following as far as applicable, the form prescribed for original applications.
Under paragraph (a) of 10 CFR 50.92, Issuance of amendment, determinations on whether to
grant a license amendment are to be guided by the considerations that govern the issuance of
initial licenses or construction permits to the extent applicable and appropriate. Both the
common standards for licenses and construction permits in paragraph (a) of 10 CFR 50.40,
Common standards, (regarding, among other things, consideration of the operating
procedures, the facility and equipment, the use of the facility, and other technical specifications,
or the proposals), and those specifically for issuance of operating licenses in paragraph (a)(3) of
10 CFR 50.57, Issuance of operating license, provide that there must be reasonable
assurance that the activities at issue will not endanger the health and safety of the public, and
that the applicant will comply with the Commissions regulations.
Section 50.36, Technical specifications, of 10 CFR establishes the regulatory requirements
related to the content of TS. The five categories of items required to be in the TS are listed in
10 CFR 50.36(c) and include (1) safety limits, limiting safety system settings, and limiting control
settings; (2) limiting conditions for operation (LCOs); (3) surveillance requirements (SRs);
(4) design features; and (5) administrative controls.

RAI 1

Issue: Amendment no. 297 to transition to permanently defueled TS deleted the several TS
related to Control Room Envelope Habitability Program (CREHP) which were the originally
adopted in amendment No 264 (TSTF-448).

        License Condition (LC) 2.c.(18)
        TS 6.20, Control Room Envelope Habitability Program
        TS 3.15.1 Emergency Control Room Air Treatment System
        SR 4.12.1.5 for the Emergency Control Room Air Treatment System

Constellation proposes not reinstating the LC stating the initial testing periodicities have been
satisfied for the control room envelope (air inleakage, habitability, and pressure) following
implementation of amendment 264. As described in amendment 264, the CREHP, in
combination with TS 4.12.1.5, was intended to:

           [ ] ensure the operability of the CRE boundary, which as part of an
           operable Emergency Control Room Air Treatment System will ensure that
           CRE habitability is maintained such that CRE occupants can control the
           reactor safely under normal conditions and maintain it in a safe condition
           following a radiological event, hazardous chemical release, or a smoke
           challenge. The program shall ensure that adequate radiation protection is
           provided to permit access and occupancy of the CRE under DBA
           conditions without personnel receiving radiation exposures in excess of 5
           rem TEDE for the duration of the accident.

Elements of the CREHP involved CRE configuration control and preventative maintenance, as
well as data collection and trending for assessment of CRE habitability and CRE boundary
operability.

Request: Considering the time between defueled operations and reinstating the CREHP:
     Provide information to justify why a new license condition with implementation
     requirements is not necessary to ensure the reinstatement of the CREHP, in combination
     with TS 4.12.1.5, would meet the intent described in amendment 264.
     Please describe how Constellation will obtain data used to determine unfiltered air
     inleakage past the CRE boundary and assess CRE habitability per TS 6.20.c and data
     used for the 24-month assessment of TS 6.20.d.

CEG Response: A new license condition is not required to ensure reinstatement of the CREHP
as the CREHP is approved and required by TSs. Periodic in-leakage testing as required by TS
6.20.c.(i) and 6.20.c.(ii) is included as approved scope to be completed prior to restoration of the
operating reactor licensing basis and technical specifications. This test will also provide the data
used for the 24-month assessment of TS 6.20.d.

RAI 2

Issue: Section 3.10 [Miscellaneous Radioactive Material Sources] of the TS was deleted by
amendment 297, which transitioned to permanently defueled technical specifications (PDTS).
The TS in this section provided specifications to assure that leakage from byproduct, source,
and special nuclear radioactive material sources does not exceed allowable limits. The staffs
justification for approving deleting Section 3.10 in the amendment 297 safety evaluation was
because the TSs did not apply to safe storage and handling of spent fuel in the spent fuel pool,
and once certifications required by 10 CFR 50.82(a)(1) are docketed, the license would no
longer authorize operation of the reactor or placement or retention of fuel in the reactor vessel,
per 10 CFR 50.82(a)(2). Constellation intends to restart the reactor and has requested an
exemption to 10 CFR 50.82(a)(2) and submitted several amendments (to include this one) to
support potential restart, and as such, the staffs previous basis for approving deletion of the TS
will no longer be valid if the restart is approved. The LAR proposes not reinstating TS 3.10 and
4.13 on the basis that the requirements are not credited in the safety analysis and not required
as they do not meet the screening criteria of 10 CFR 50.36(c)(2)(ii). The phrase not credited in
the safety analysis does not explicitly state whether the safety analysis referred to is only for
shutdown or if the phrase was meant to include those analyses for operations.

Request: Please provide further detailed discussion clarifying which analysis/analyses support
these statements to not reinstate TS 3.10 and TS 4.13. Specify whether the safety analysis
refers only to shutdown conditions or includes operational analyses.

CEG Response: The statements not credited in any safety analysis and not credited in the
safety analysis provided in Reference 1 (ML25212A076) apply to the operational Design Basis
Accidents (DBA) or Transients identified in Chapter 14 of the proposed Crane UFSAR. The
proposed Chapter 14 DBAs and Transients are presented in Table 3.1.1: CCEC DBAs and
Transients of Attachment 1 of Reference 1. As stated in Attachment 1 of Reference 1, sealed
radioactive material sources are controlled under a licensee-controlled program and in
accordance with regulatory requirements.

RAI 3

Issue: Amendment no. 297 deleted PDTS TS 3/4.1.4, Handling of Irradiated Fuel with Fuel
Handling Building Crane, previously TS 3.11, Handling of Irradiated Fuel. Constellation
proposes not reinstating TS 3.11 because the crane has been replaced with a single-failure-
proof crane. The [original] Fuel Handling Building Crane remains on site. Constellation has not
proposed a new TS requirement for the single-failure-proof crane or controls to prevent use of
the [original] Fuel Handling Building Crane for functions that would necessitate a TS.

Request: Please provide justification for not including TS requirements for the non-single-
failure-proof crane.

CEG Response: MIS-A-2 is a non-single-failure proof crane that is administratively prevented
from being used in or over the spent fuel pool thus precluding the potential for a cask-drop
accident in the spent fuel pool when using this crane. These administrative controls are being
incorporated into station procedures and section 9.7 of the UFSAR.

Proposed change to UFSAR Section 9.7.2 [New language is in italics]

     The original FHB crane (MIS-A-2) is positioned south of the replacement FHB
     crane (MIS-A-2B) on the common FHB crane runway although no longer used
     north of the FHB truck bay (over the spent fuel pool) or over spent fuel casks.
     Administrative controls prevent operation of both cranes concurrently and
     maintain 10-ft separation between the two cranes to limit the loading on the
     structure.

     Technical Specification (TS) Amendment 300 (ML20297A635) removed TS
     requirements associated with handling of irradiated fuel with the fuel handling
     building crane. Removal of these TSs was approved based on MIS-A-2B
     meeting the requirements of NUREG-0554 (Reference 27) for a single failure
     proof crane. Although MIS-A-2 remains installed and available for use, MIS-A-
     2 does not satisfy the requirements for a single failure proof crane in
     accordance with the guidelines of Reference 27. Accordingly, operation of
     MIS-A-2 is administratively prevented from use over the spent fuel pools or for
     any spent fuel handling operations.

RAI 4

Issue: Section 6.11 of the TS, Radiation Protection Program, was deleted by amendment 297,
which transitioned to permanently defueled technical specifications. The NRC staffs justification
for approval was the same as described above for TS 3.10, and similarly, may no longer be
valid if restart of CCEC is approved. The LAR proposes not reinstating the TS on the basis that
the Radiation Monitoring Program is not required per 10 CFR 50.36, and therefore not required
to be in the TS.

Request: Please provide a clarification as to whether or not the requirements in TS 6.11 are
needed for safe operation of the facility as an operational site, as opposed to a site in
decommissioning.

CEG Response: TS 6.11 is applicable to procedures which implement the requirements of 10
CFR Part 20. As 10 CFR Part 20 Subpart B, Radiation Protection Programs, is applicable to
both an operational site as well as a site in decommissioning, the requirements previously
described in TS 6.11 are applicable to both the operational site and a site in decommissioning.
However, as discussed in the LAR that removed 6.11 from TSs, the program is not necessary to
assure operation of the facility in a safe manner and can be relocated from the TS to the
UFSAR. The requirement to have procedures to implement 10 CFR Part 20 and the
requirement for periodic review of these procedures is addressed under 10 CFR 20 Subpart B 
Radiation Protection Programs. This statement does not distinguish between an operational
site or a site in decommissioning as the regulations are applicable to both.

Additionally, there is no corresponding TS in NUREG-1430 Volume 1, Revision 5, Standard
Technical Specifications for Babcock and Wilcox Plants.

RAI 9

Issue: In some instances, TS requirements can be found to be non-conservative. In some of
these cases, plant operation can continue if administrative controls are used to address non-
conservative TS requirements, provided the TS are amended in a time frame commensurate
with the safety significance of the non-conservatism.

Request: Please describe any non-conservative TS requirements that existed during the last
operating cycle and how proposed TS will eliminate these non-conservatisms.

CEG Response: In 2012, River water level at intake structure (TS 3.14.2) was identified in IR
5000289/2011005 as a non-conservative TS (NCTS) based on an error between river water
level and the corresponding flow rate. A LAR was submitted in 2013 to correct the NCTS but
was later withdrawn based on open actions associated with industry response to the Fukushima
event.

With this response, CEG is correcting the error documented in IR 5000289/2011005 with a
proposed revision to TS 3.14.2.

Proposed TS 3.14.2:

           3.14.2     OPERATING LIMIT FOR FLOOD

           Applicability

           POWER OPERATION or HOT STANDBY

           Objective

           To define the action taken in the event river elevation challenges the flood
           protection dike

           Specification

           3.14.2.1 If the river level reaches 300 feet elevation then the unit will be
           placed in HOT SHUTDOWN within 2 hours.

           Bases

           This Technical Specification requires a plant shutdown if the flood level
           reaches the protection of the dike. The dike elevation at the River Water
           Intake Structure is 305 feet (Reference 1). The minimum dike elevation is
           at the downstream end of the plant site, at which point the dike elevation
           is 304 feet (Reference 1). Placing the unit in HOT SHUTDOWN when the
           river level reaches 300 feet elevation at the River Water Intake Structure
           provides an adequate margin to ensure the reactor is shutdown before
           the river water level exceeds the dike.

           References

           (1) UFSAR, Section 2.6.5  Design of Hydraulic Facilities

Technical Justification:

The Crane probabilistic risk assessment identified river flooding as a large contributor to overall
plant risk. ln 2011, to better quantify the flood risk, CEG updated the original licensing basis
flooding analysis.

C-1101-122-E410-003, "River Stage Discharge and Discharge Frequency Analysis" Rev. 0,
concluded that although the frequency for severe flooding decreased, the predicted maximum
flood (PMF) height would be greater, by approximately 3.5 feet (i.e., a reference value of 313.5
ft).

As a result, CEG initiated IR 01268247 to assess the site impact and take appropriate corrective
actions. The actions to address the new PMF height have been completed. However, Inspection
Report 5000289/2011005 (ML12039A087) identified a Severity Level IV Non-Cited Violation
associated with 10 CFR 50, Appendix B, Criterion XVI, Corrective Actions, because CEG did not
identify and correct a condition adverse to quality regarding the impact of the revised river stage
discharge analysis result on Technical Specifications (TSs). Specifically, CEG did not recognize
that the revised river discharge analysis resulted in a lower flow-based river shutdown level,
resulting in a non-conservative TS.

TSs and the UFSAR identify the design flood is an event with a river flow of 1,100,000 CFS. The
new analysis does not alter the conclusion that the dike will protect the site during such an
event.

TS 3.14.2 directs operators to initiate a plant shutdown (place the unit in Hot Shutdown) before
river water level / flow exceeds the height of the protective dikes at the River Water Intake
Structure. The river water level stated in TS 3.14.2, 302 feet, was based on a corresponding
design bases flow of 1,000,000 cfs. The 2011 analysis determined that the level associated with
1,000,000 cfs was actually 299.8 feet. The NCTS was based on the fact that if the operators
initiated a plant shut down at 302 ft, the 1,100,000 cfs would have been exceeded.

The Crane dike system, as described in UFSAR section 2.6.5, is such that the dikes provide
adequate protection from a flood with a flowrate of 1,100,000 cfs. with several feet of margin.

TS 3.14.2 is being revised to direct operators to initiate a plant shut down based on river water
level of 300 feet at the River Water Intake Structure. The basis is being clarified to align the
action with the observable level at the River Water Intake Structure.

 1.4.2   REACTOR PROTECTION SYSTEM

The reactor protection system is described in Section 7.1 of the Updated FSAR. It is that
combination of protection channels and associated circuitry which forms the automatic system
that protects the reactor by control rod trip. It includes the four protection channels, their
associated instrument channel inputs, manual trip switch, all rod drive control protection trip
breakers, and activating relays or coils.

1.4.3   PROTECTION CHANNEL

A PROTECTION CHANNEL as described in Section 7.1 of the updated FSAR (one of three or
one of four independent channels, complete with sensors, sensor power supply units, amplifiers,
and bistable modules provided for every reactor protection safety parameter) is a combination of
instrument channels forming a single digital output to the protection system's coincidence logic.
It includes a shutdown bypass circuit, a protection channel bypass circuit and a reactor trip
module.

1.4.4   REACTOR PROTECTION SYSTEM LOGIC

This system utilizes reactor trip module relays (coils and contacts) in all four of the protection
channels as described in Section 7.1 of the updated FSAR, to provide reactor trip signals for de-
energizing the six four control rod drive trip breakers. The control rod drive trip breakers are
arranged to provide a one-out-of-two-times-two logic. Each element of the
one-out-of-two-times-two logic is controlled by a separate set of two-out-of-four logic contacts
from the four reactor protection channels.

1.4.5   ENGINEERED SAFETY FEATURES SYSTEM

This system utilizes relay contact output from individual channels arranged in three analog sub-
systems and two two-out-of-three logic sub-systems as shown in Figure 7.1-4 of the updated
FSAR. The logic sub-system is wired to provide appropriate signals for the actuation of
redundant engineered safety features equipment on a two-of-three basis for any given
parameter.

1.4.6   DEGREE OF REDUNDANCY

The difference between the number of operable channels and the number of channels which,
when tripped, will cause an automatic system trip.

1.5     INSTRUMENTATION SURVEILLANCE

1.5.1   TRIP TEST

A TRIP TEST is a test of logic elements in a protection channel to verify their associated trip
action.

 1.4.2   REACTOR PROTECTION SYSTEM

The reactor protection system is described in Section 7.1 of the Updated FSAR. It is that
combination of protection channels and associated circuitry which forms the automatic system
that protects the reactor by control rod trip. It includes the four protection channels, their
associated instrument channel inputs, manual trip switch, all rod drive control protection trip
breakers, and activating relays or coils.

1.4.3   PROTECTION CHANNEL

A PROTECTION CHANNEL as described in Section 7.1 of the updated FSAR (one of three or
one of four independent channels, complete with sensors, sensor power supply units, amplifiers,
and bistable modules provided for every reactor protection safety parameter) is a combination of
instrument channels forming a single digital output to the protection system's coincidence logic.
It includes a shutdown bypass circuit, a protection channel bypass circuit and a reactor trip
module.

1.4.4   REACTOR PROTECTION SYSTEM LOGIC

This system utilizes reactor trip module relays (coils and contacts) in all four of the protection
channels as described in Section 7.1 of the updated FSAR, to provide reactor trip signals for de-
energizing the four control rod drive trip breakers. The control rod drive trip breakers are
arranged to provide a one-out-of-two-times-two logic. Each element of the
one-out-of-two-times-two logic is controlled by a separate set of two-out-of-four logic contacts
from the four reactor protection channels.

1.4.5   ENGINEERED SAFETY FEATURES SYSTEM

This system utilizes relay contact output from individual channels arranged in three analog sub-
systems and two two-out-of-three logic sub-systems as shown in Figure 7.1-4 of the updated
FSAR. The logic sub-system is wired to provide appropriate signals for the actuation of
redundant engineered safety features equipment on a two-of-three basis for any given
parameter.

1.4.6   DEGREE OF REDUNDANCY

The difference between the number of operable channels and the number of channels which,
when tripped, will cause an automatic system trip.

1.5     INSTRUMENTATION SURVEILLANCE

1.5.1   TRIP TEST

A TRIP TEST is a test of logic elements in a protection channel to verify their associated trip
action.
